test.name: Two macOS accounts: the second account cannot reach the first account's daemon

expected: a second macOS account on this Mac cannot open the first account's daemon socket (permission denied at the path), and its own stacklyd runs with its own socket and roots
reason: this Mac has one login account (ojiepermana, uid 502; `dscl . -list /Users UniqueID` lists no other uid from 500 up), and creating a second macOS account needs an administrator password and a GUI login, which the user's policy records as a heavy manual step; the automated part of AC-2 passes: a listener with the expected uid set to another uid refuses a real client with ipc.peer_rejected, and a failing PeerCredSource refuses too (crates/ipc/tests/transport, listener::)
owner: ojiepermana (the user): add a second standard account on this Mac, then run the steps below and turn this into a new PASS or FAIL record
steps: create a second standard macOS account on this Mac and log in to it once
as the first account, start `stacklyd` (no STACKLY_ROOT) and note the socket path from `stackly daemon status`

as the second account, try to reach the first account's socket path with `ls -l <path>` and `nc -U <path>`: expect permission denied at the path, because the first account's runtime root is 0700 and its socket 0600
as the second account, start its own `stacklyd`: expect its own socket under its own temporary folder and its own roots under its home, and `stackly daemon status` there shows the second daemon
stop both daemons and record PASS or FAIL in a new record with `cargo xtask evidence new`
